title: The Spiders Unilluminable home
author: George Tokarsky
shortDescription:
The Tokarsky-Marinov Project: Bhavya Jain

In this spiders unilluminable home, all the walls are viewed as mirrors and an unilluminable point is at its center and four other unilluminable points are the middle points of the four long walls. If a light is placed at the center then all of its light rays will never come back to itself or reach any of the four middle points. We magnify only middle of the left and the right long walls and the center.

We made this unilluminable room using a square ABCD where all vertices are 90 degrees.

If you want to create unilluminable rooms using a square ABCD the rules are very simple and you can find them in Tokarsky's paper at https://doi.org/10.1080/00029890.1995....  

Here are the rules 
1.take a square ABCD in which the angle A is 90 degrees which must divide 90 and all other angles are 90 since they are integer multiples of A
2.make an unilluminable room by forming mirror images of ABCD and the key is that every point labelled B,C or D must form a corner and voila any point labelled A is an unilluminable point whether it is a corner or not.

You can make and send your own rooms to Bhavya at [redacted-email]
